s: Which of the following statements regarding the India–US trade deal is incorrect?
o: The additional 25% punitive duty imposed over Russian oil purchases was removed.
India has regained Generalised System of Preferences (GSP), which was withdrawn in 2019.
India is expected to make purchases of up to USD 500 billion of US energy, agriculture, coal and technology.
Mission 500 aims to raise bilateral trade to USD 500 billion by 2030.
x: India has not regained GSP; it was withdrawn in 2019. The other statements correctly describe the removal of the additional 25% duty, expected purchases of up to USD 500 billion, and the Mission 500 target of USD 500 billion by 2030.

s: Amid US pressure on India's purchases of Russian oil, what did Donald Trump claim India had agreed to do under the India–US trade understanding?
o: Withdraw from the India–Russia strategic partnership
x: Donald Trump claimed that India had agreed to stop buying Russian oil under the India–US trade understanding. The claim concerned Russian oil purchases, not India's strategic partnership with Russia or its purchases from the United States.

s: Under the India–US trade deal, what will be the effective tariff burden on Indian goods, compared with the pre-deal level?
x: The effective burden is reduced from about 50% to 18%. The figure of 20% refers to the approximate tariff faced by Vietnam and Bangladesh, while 30–35% refers to China.

s: Which of the following groups was fully protected under the agricultural provisions of the India–US trade agreement?
o: Aircraft parts, generic drugs and diamonds
Dairy, poultry, meat and GM foods
x: Dairy, poultry, meat and GM foods were among the agricultural items fully protected. Spices, tea, coffee and cashew were among the exports facing zero additional duty, while the other options refer to industrial or non-agricultural sectors.

s: Which country saw a tariff on Indian goods reduced from 50 percent to 18 percent under the February 2026 trade deal?
x: Under the February 2026 India-US trade deal, the US tariff on India was reduced from 50 percent to 18 percent.

s: Which pre-deal Indian measure opened the nuclear sector to private players?
x: The SHANTI Act, 2025, opened India’s nuclear sector to private players. US–India COMPACT concerned military partnership, commerce and technology, while iCET concerned technology cooperation.

s: What is the full form of US–India COMPACT announced in 2025?
o: Coordinated Mechanism for Public Administration, Commerce & Technology
Comprehensive Organisation for Market Partnership, Agriculture, Commerce & Trade
Catalyzing Operations for Maritime Partnership, Accelerated Cooperation & Transport
Catalyzing Opportunities for Military Partnership, Accelerated Commerce & Technology
x: US–India COMPACT stands for Catalyzing Opportunities for Military Partnership, Accelerated Commerce & Technology. The other expansions do not correspond to the 2025 bilateral framework.

s: By which year does India–US 'Mission 500' aim at bilateral trade of USD 500 billion?
x: Mission 500 targets USD 500 billion of India–US trade by 2030.

s: What happened to India's GSP benefits, withdrawn in 2019, under the February 2026 India–US trade deal?
x: The deal did not restore GSP; the US tariff on India is now 18%, not zero.

s: Which rank does the United States hold among investors in India, with USD 70.65 billion during 2000–2025?
x: The US is the 3rd largest investor in India, with about USD 70.65 billion of investment from 2000 to 2025.

s: The world's fastest cruise missile BrahMos gets its name from
o: Brahma, the God of creation, and Moses, the Biblical prophet
The Indian river Brahmaputra and the Russian river Moskva
Brahma, the Indian god, and the Russian river Moskva
The river Brahmaputra and Moses, the Biblical prophet
x: BrahMos is a portmanteau combining the Indian river Brahmaputra and the Russian river Moskva, reflecting the joint India-Russia development of the missile.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India–Russia economic ties?
o: They set a trade target of USD 100 billion by 2030.
India–Russia trade stood at USD 128 billion in 2024–25.
They set a target of USD 50 billion in mutual investment by 2025.
After 2022, Russia became India's largest crude supplier.
x: India–Russia trade was USD 68.72 billion in 2024–25; USD 128 billion is roughly India–US trade.

s: What position did Russia attain among India's crude-oil suppliers after 2022?
x: After 2022, Russia became India's largest crude supplier.

s: In which year were India–Russia ties upgraded to a 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership'?
x: The upgrade came in 2010; 2000 saw the Declaration on Strategic Partnership.

s: Which development was reported regarding Kudankulam Units 1–6 during 2025?
o: All six units were permanently shut down after the delivery of Unit 6
The Unit 6 reactor vessel was delivered, alongside talks on SMRs and Units 7–8
Units 7–8 were commissioned and the Unit 6 reactor vessel was exported
Only Units 1–2 remained operational and talks on SMRs were abandoned
x: In 2025, the Unit 6 reactor vessel was delivered at Kudankulam, while talks continued on SMRs and Units 7–8. The other options reverse or alter these developments.

s: Where was WAVES 2025, attended by Russian Culture Minister Olga Lyubimova in May 2025, held?
x: Olga Lyubimova attended WAVES 2025 in Mumbai in May 2025.

s: At the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit held in New Delhi in December 2025, India and Russia set which trade target for 2030?
x: India and Russia set a bilateral trade target of 100 billion dollars by 2030.

s: Which of the following is among the India–Russia connectivity initiatives?
x: The Chennai–Vladivostok maritime corridor is an India–Russia connectivity initiative, along with INSTC (India–Iran–Russia) and the proposed India–EAEU FTA. The other options are not India–Russia connectivity projects.

s: Which project is described as a flagship of India–Russia nuclear cooperation?
x: The Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant is the flagship of India–Russia nuclear cooperation. BrahMos concerns co-development, Sakhalin concerns energy investment, and INDRA is an exercise.

s: Through which Russian agency did India sign the 'Action Plan for Prioritization and Implementation of Cooperation Areas in the Nuclear Field'?
x: The nuclear-field Action Plan was signed with Russia through Rosatom.

s: BrahMos is named after the Brahmaputra and which Russian river?
x: BrahMos takes its name from the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.

s: Which of the following is a joint India–Russia development rather than a purchase or licence build?
x: BrahMos is jointly developed by DRDO and NPO Mashinostroyeniya; S-400 and INS Vikramaditya are purchases and Su-30MKI is licence-built by HAL.

s: Of the five S-400 Triumf regiments India purchased from Russia, how many had been delivered?
x: India bought 5 S-400 regiments, of which 3 have been delivered.

s: Which company makes the AK-203 rifles under India–Russia cooperation?
x: AK-203 is made by Indo-Russia Rifles Pvt Ltd; HAL licence-builds the Su-30MKI.

s: Annual India–Russia summits began with which development?
o: 1971 Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation
x: Annual summits began with the 2000 Declaration on Strategic Partnership; the 2010 upgrade was to a Special and Privileged one.

s: Which countries are linked by the International North–South Transport Corridor (INSTC)?
x: The INSTC is a multi-modal corridor connecting India, Iran and Russia.

s: In which year did India sign the Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation with the USSR?
x: The Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation was signed in 1971; annual summits began only after the 2000 Strategic Partnership.

s: India’s Free Trade Agreement concluded in December 2025 marked its first FTA with which country?
x: The agreement concluded in December 2025 was India’s first FTA with New Zealand and was negotiated in a record nine months by a women-led team. Australia, China and Japan are listed as ASEAN FTA partners, but the agreement in question was with New Zealand.

s: Under the India–New Zealand FTA, India offered tariff relief on what share of New Zealand imports?
x: India offered tariff relief on 95% of New Zealand imports, 57% duty-free from day one; New Zealand gave zero duty on 100% of Indian exports.

s: Which of the following statements regarding products excluded by India from the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement is incorrect?
o: Dairy products such as milk, cheese, butter and yogurt were excluded.
x: Kiwifruit was not listed among the products excluded by India; it was identified under agricultural cooperation. Dairy products, onions and edible oils were among the exclusions.

s: Which of the following pairs of trade-agreement type and feature is correctly matched?
o: Partial Scope Agreement – Free movement of capital and labour
Free Trade Agreement – Common external tariff
x: A Customs Union adds a common external tariff. A Partial Scope Agreement covers limited goods, an FTA cuts tariffs among members while keeping own tariffs for others, and a Common Market adds free movement of capital and labour.

s: Under the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, what FDI commitment did New Zealand make?
x: New Zealand committed to invest $20 billion over 15 years, with a clawback provision.

s: Which Arab state has started first nuclear power plant?
x: The Barakah Nuclear Power Plant (NPP), the first in the UAE and the Arab World, began operating in 2020. Three reactors are currently in operation and one is close to construction completion. The NPP is expected to provide up to 25 percent of the country’s electricity with the capacity to power more than half a million Emirate households – when it becomes fully operational in the coming years.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 'Shadbhujii Coalition'?
o: It includes Greece and Cyprus along with India
IMEC was announced at the 2023 G20
It was announced by Israel's President Isaac Herzog
x: The coalition was announced by PM Benjamin Netanyahu, not President Isaac Herzog.

s: In which year did India recognise Israel?
x: India recognised Israel in 1950. The year 1992 refers to the establishment of full diplomatic ties, while the other years do not match the stated recognition milestone.

s: In which year did the India–UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) come into force?
x: The CEPA came into force in 2022; the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership dates to 2017.

s: During Operation Swadesh, about how many Indian medical students were estimated to be in Iran?
x: Around 10,000 Indians were in Iran, including 2,500–3,000 medical students.

s: Over what period did Israel target 50,000 more Indian workers after PM Modi's visit?
x: The target of 50,000 more Indian workers is for five years, not ten.

s: During Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan's visit to India, agreements covered which of the following sectors?
o: Agriculture, fisheries, tourism, textiles and banking
Nuclear energy, energy, railways, space and artificial intelligence
Defence, education, health, mining and aviation
Water, shipping, forests, sports and culture
x: The agreements covered nuclear energy, energy, railways, space and artificial intelligence. The other combinations do not represent the sectors identified for the visit.

s: Which country is a member of the I2U2 grouping along with India, Israel and the USA?
x: I2U2 = India, Israel, UAE and USA.

s: From which country did India evacuate its nationals under Operation Swadesh (January 2026)?
x: Operation Swadesh evacuated Indians from Iran amid anti-government protests.

s: Into which type of partnership were India–Israel ties expanded during PM Modi's historic visit to Israel?
x: PM Modi's visit expanded India–Israel ties into a Special Strategic Partnership, centred on peace, innovation and prosperity.

s: Which was the first Arab country to have a nuclear power plant?
x: The UAE's Barakah nuclear plant, working since 2020, made it the first Arab state with nuclear power.

s: In which year did India establish full diplomatic relations with Israel?
x: India recognised Israel in 1950 but set up full diplomatic ties only in 1992.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India recognised Israel in 1950.
2. India established full diplomatic ties with Israel in 1992.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: recognition came in 1950 and full diplomatic ties in 1992.

s: During the US military action in Venezuela in early January 2026, who were seized by US special forces in Caracas?
x: US special forces seized President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores; Delcy Rodríguez then became interim president.

s: The UN Secretary-General called the US military action in Venezuela a 'dangerous precedent' because it had no mandate from which body?
x: The action lacked a UN Security Council mandate, which is why it was called a dangerous precedent.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the January 2026 US action in Venezuela?
o: Nicolás Maduro was first taken to the USS Iwo Jima
Maduro was detained in New York on narco-terrorism charges
Delcy Rodríguez was sworn in as Interim President after being named by Venezuelan courts
Venezuela described the action as a lawful extradition
x: Venezuela called the action a “kidnapping” and declared a state of external disturbance.

s: Which of the following doctrine pairs is correctly matched?
o: Truman Doctrine – Opposed European interference in the Americas
Roosevelt Corollary – Expansion of the Monroe Doctrine in 1904
'Don-roe Doctrine' – Articulated by James Monroe in 1823
x: The Roosevelt Corollary expanded the Monroe Doctrine in 1904. The Monroe Doctrine (1823) opposed European interference, the Truman Doctrine meant Cold War containment and 'Don-roe' refers to its revival.

s: In which year was the Monroe Doctrine, invoked by the United States over Venezuela, proclaimed?
x: The Monroe Doctrine was enunciated in 1823.

s: Under what circumstances did Delcy Rodríguez become interim President of Venezuela in January 2026?
o: Nicolás Maduro resigned after an election defeat
the United States seized Nicolás Maduro
the National Assembly impeached Nicolás Maduro
x: Delcy Rodríguez became interim President after the United States seized Nicolás Maduro.

s: What is the currency of Venezuela?
x: Venezuela's currency is the bolívar; the country is an OPEC member with the largest proven crude reserves.

s: The India–Nepal environment MoU focuses on conservation in which regions?
x: The MoU focuses on the Himalayan and Terai regions and covers forestry, wildlife, biodiversity and climate change.

s: Tarique Rahman was sworn in as Prime Minister of which country on 17 February 2026?
x: Tarique Rahman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party was sworn in as Prime Minister of Bangladesh on 17 February 2026 after the parliamentary election.

s: Who was Nepal's Prime Minister when the India–Nepal Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty on criminal matters was signed?
x: Sushila Karki is Nepal's Prime Minister; Ram Chandra Poudel is the President.

s: What was the value of the aid package for Seychelles announced by PM Modi after talks with President Dr Patrick Herminie?
x: India announced a $175 million aid package for Seychelles.

s: With which Indian vision was the $175 million aid package to Seychelles linked?
x: The Seychelles package was linked to Vision MAHASAGAR, which extends SAGAR (2015).

s: India's USD 450 million package for Sri Lanka after Cyclone Ditwah included how much as concessional credit?
x: The package had USD 350 million in concessional credit and USD 100 million in grants.

s: What was the name of India's relief operation that delivered more than 1,100 tonnes of relief on the day of Cyclone Ditwah?
x: Operation Sagar Bandhu delivered more than 1,100 tonnes of relief on the day of Cyclone Ditwah. The other operation names are not associated with this relief effort in the stated information.

s: The Ganga Water Sharing Treaty, signed in 1996, is scheduled to expire in which month and year?
x: The Ganga Water Sharing Treaty was signed on 12 December 1996 for 30 years and is scheduled to expire in December 2026. December 1996 was the month and year of signing, not its expiry.

s: What is the full form of SAGAR (2015), India's maritime vision for the Indian Ocean Region?
o: Safety and Growth Across the Region
Security and Governance for All in the Region
Sustainable Growth for All in the Region
Security and Growth for All in the Region
x: SAGAR stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region and casts India as a net security provider in the IOR.

s: What is the installed capacity of the Wangchhu Hydroelectric Project in Bhutan, on which the Adani Group began work?
x: Wangchhu has an installed capacity of 570 MW (4 × 142.5 MW).

s: On which date did India and Pakistan first exchange lists of nuclear installations?
x: The agreement was signed on 31 December 1988; the first exchange took place on 1 January 1992.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ganga Water Sharing Treaty:
1. It governs dry-season flows at Farakka in West Bengal.
2. Earlier temporary arrangements were made in 1977, 1982 and 1986.
3. It can be renewed without mutual consent.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct. The earlier arrangements were in 1977, 1982 and 1985, and renewal requires mutual consent.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Wangchhu Hydroelectric Project in Bhutan?
o: The Wangchu is called Raidak in India
It supplies winter power to India
The Wangchu is a tributary of the Brahmaputra
x: It is reversed: winter power goes to Bhutan and the summer surplus to India.

s: In which year was MAHASAGAR, which extends SAGAR to the Global South and the Indo-Pacific, announced?
x: SAGAR dates to 2015; MAHASAGAR (2025) extends it to the Global South and Indo-Pacific.

s:
Consider the following statements about SAGAR:
1. It was announced in 2015.
2. It projects India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region, 2015) casts India as net security provider in the IOR.

s: What share does Druk Green Power hold in the joint venture for Bhutan's Wangchhu project?
x: The JV is Druk Green Power 51% and Adani Power 49%.

s: Who founded the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in 1978?
x: The BNP, which won the February 2026 election, was founded in 1978 by Ziaur Rahman.

s: What is the approximate length of the India–Bangladesh border?
x: India shares about 4,096 km of border with Bangladesh, its longest land border.

s: For how many years was the Ganga Water Sharing Treaty signed on 12 December 1996?
x: The treaty was signed for 30 years, so it expires in December 2026.

s: Which of the following countries was among the 23 countries with which India signed MoUs on Digital Public Infrastructure and India Stack?
x: Mongolia was among the countries included in India’s Digital Public Infrastructure and India Stack MoUs. The United Arab Emirates, Bhutan and France were associated with UPI availability, not the specified MoU list.

s: What new dialogue framework was established in the India–Canada reset?
o: A new G7-level trade dialogue framework
A new NSA-level security dialogue framework
x: The India–Canada reset included a new NSA-level security dialogue framework. The other three options are not the framework identified in the bilateral reset.

s: In which year was NATO, headquartered in Brussels, established, and who is its Secretary-General from 1 October 2024?
x: NATO was established in 1949, is headquartered in Brussels, and Mark Rutte is Secretary-General from 1 October 2024.

s: By which year have India and Canada set a CEPA target of USD 70 billion?
x: The India–Canada CEPA target is USD 70 billion by 2030.

s: When did Mark Carney become Prime Minister of Canada?
x: Carney became PM in March 2025 after Justin Trudeau stepped down in January 2025.

s: Which of the following is a Partner, not a Guest, in the US-led PAX SILICA initiative?
x: The UK and Japan are Partners; Taiwan, Canada and the EU are Guests.

s: Where did the European Union set up its first 'Legal Gateway' office outside its member countries?
x: The EU's first Legal Gateway office outside its member states is in New Delhi, guiding Indians on legal migration to the 27 EU states.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Digital Public Infrastructure outreach?
o: India signed DPI or India Stack MoUs with 23 countries
DigiLocker pacts covered Cuba, Kenya, the UAE and Lao PDR
The India Stack Global Portal offered 18 platforms
x: UPI was available in eight countries, not 23; 23 is the number of countries with DPI or India Stack MoUs.

s: Who launched Arctic Sentry for security in the Arctic and the High North?
x: NATO launched Arctic Sentry; it is not a military operation with permanent troops.

s: With reference to NATO's Arctic Sentry, which pair is correctly matched?
x: Denmark's Arctic Endurance is associated with Greenland. Cold Response is Norway's, Joint Force Command Norfolk is in the USA, and Arctic Sentry coordinates with both exercises.

s: Which group of countries condemned the United States military action in Venezuela in January 2026?
o: Japan, Australia, New Zealand and South Korea
x: Russia, China, Iran and Cuba condemned the US military action in Venezuela, while the EU urged restraint. The other options list countries not identified as the condemning group.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Weimar Triangle?
o: It consists of France, Germany and Poland
It was established on 29 August 1991 at Weimar
It has a formal institutional structure
S. Jaishankar's meeting with it was India's first-ever engagement
x: The Weimar Triangle has no formal institutional structure.

s: By how many years was the India–Fiji Agriculture MoU extended at the talks of 9 January 2026?
x: The MoU was extended by five years and a Joint Working Group was to be set up.

s: Who leads PAX SILICA, the initiative to secure supply chains in silicon, semiconductors, AI and critical minerals?
x: PAX SILICA is a US-led initiative covering these sectors.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the G7?
x: The G7 is Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, UK and US; Russia was in the G8 from 1998.

s: Hardeep Nijjar, whose killing triggered the 2023 India–Canada crisis, was killed in which Canadian province?
x: The Nijjar killing (June 2023) took place in British Columbia, not Ontario.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2023 India–Canada diplomatic crisis?
o: Justin Trudeau alleged an Indian role in the killing of Hardeep Nijjar.
Diplomats were expelled and High Commissioners withdrawn.
The alleged killing took place in Ontario.
The crisis followed an allegation by Canada's Prime Minister.
x: The case was linked to British Columbia, not Ontario; the other statements are correct.

s: Students from which country form the largest international student group in Canada?
x: Indian students (3.92 lakh in December 2024) are the largest international student group in Canada.

s: In which year did the G7 become the G8 with the inclusion of Russia?
x: Russia joined in 1998, making the G7 the G8.

s: Where was the World Economic Forum, whose President Børge Brende resigned over Epstein links, established in 1971?
x: The WEF was established in 1971 at Cologny in Geneva.

s: Who became the youngest Prime Minister in Dutch history in February 2026?
x: Rob Jetten, a member of D66, became the youngest Prime Minister in Dutch history at the age of 38. Andrey Gurov became Bulgaria's interim Prime Minister, while Anutin Charnvirakul and Tariq Rahman are associated with Thailand and Bangladesh respectively.

s: By whom was José María Balkazar of Peru Libre elected as Peru's president?
x: Balkazar was elected by Peru's 130-member Congress.

s: Who was Japan's Prime Minister when Japan issued an alert after North Korean missile launches in January 2026?
x: Sanae Takaichi was the Prime Minister of Japan at the time.

s: In the February 2026 Japanese election, the LDP won how many of the 465 seats?
x: The LDP won 271 of 465 seats (majority mark 261); Thailand's Bhumjaithai won 194 of 500.

s: Andrey Gurov was appointed interim Prime Minister of which country?
x: Andrey Gurov, Deputy Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, was appointed Bulgaria's interim PM by President Iliana Lotova.

s: Mia Amor Mottley, who won a third term in February 2026 by winning all 30 seats, is the Prime Minister of which country?
x: Mia Amor Mottley of the Barbados Labour Party won all 30 seats and a third term in Barbados.

s: Which former President of South Korea was sentenced to life imprisonment over the martial law of 3 December 2024?
x: Ex-President Yoon Suk Yeol got life imprisonment for declaring martial law on 3 December 2024.

s: Which party, led by caretaker PM Anutin Charnvirakul, emerged as the largest party in Thailand's February 2026 election?
x: Bhumjaithai won 194 of 500 seats, ahead of the People's Party (116) and Pheu Thai (76).

s: What is RELOS, signed between India and Russia in February 2025 and operationalised in June 2026?
x: RELOS is the India–Russia logistics pact, signed in February 2025 and operationalised in June 2026.

s: Where was the 13th edition of the multilateral naval exercise MILAN (February 2026) hosted?
x: MILAN 2026 was held at Visakhapatnam on 15–25 February 2026 along with the International Fleet Review.

s: Exercise Dharma Guardian 2026, held at Chaubattia in Uttarakhand, is an Army exercise between India and which country?
x: Dharma Guardian is the India–Japan Army exercise; INDRA is the India–Russia series.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Zapad-2025 was hosted by Russia; India only took part in it.

s: Which period does the India–Russia military-technical cooperation agreement cover?
x: The India–Russia military-technical cooperation agreement covers 2021–2031.

s: By which year have India and the UAE set a target of USD 200 billion in bilateral trade?
x: The India–UAE bilateral trade target is USD 200 billion by 2032.

s: Venezuela possesses approximately how many barrels of proven crude oil reserves?
x: Venezuela has approximately 300 billion barrels of proven crude reserves.

s: What was the status of the Kartarpur Corridor after Operation Sindoor in May 2025?
o: It was transferred to the United Nations.
It was declared a non-binding protocol.
x: The Kartarpur Corridor, which had opened in 2019, was suspended after Operation Sindoor in May 2025. The 2019 opening is its earlier status, not the post-Operation Sindoor development.

s: Operation Sindoor was India's response to the terror attack on tourists at which place?
x: Operation Sindoor followed the Pahalgam terror attack and involved overt military action against Pakistan-based terror infrastructure.

s: Who led the Operation Sindoor outreach delegation (May 2025) that included AP MP Daggubati Purandeswari?
x: Purandeswari was in Ravi Shankar Prasad's delegation; Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu went with Supriya Sule and GM Harish Balayogi with Shashi Tharoor.

s: Under Operation Sindoor (6-7 May 2025), how many terror camps in Pakistan and PoK did India strike?
x: Operation Sindoor struck nine terror camps after the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025.

s: For which occasion were Sikh jathas denied permission to visit Nankana Sahib in November 2025?
o: The opening anniversary of the Kartarpur Corridor
x: The denied Sikh jathas were intended to visit Nankana Sahib for Guru Nanak's birth anniversary in November 2025. Maharaja Ranjit Singh's death anniversary was a separate occasion linked to the earlier denial in June 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India–Pakistan religious-visit framework?
o: Nankana Sahib, in Pakistan's Punjab, is the birthplace of Guru Nanak
The Simla Agreement of 1972 has a non-binding exchanges clause
The 1974 Protocol covers Nankana Sahib and Ajmer Sharif
x: Katas Raj is in Punjab; it is Shadani Darbar that is in Sindh.

s: Who were the two US officials associated with the May 2025 India–Pakistan ceasefire announcement?
o: Vice President Marco Rubio and Secretary of State J.D. Vance
Vice President J.D. Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio
Vice President J.D. Vance and Secretary of State Donald Trump
Vice President Marco Rubio and Secretary of State Donald Trump
x: The US officials were Vice President J.D. Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The other options incorrectly interchange the offices or include Donald Trump instead of one of the two officials identified.

s: Who is Pakistan's army chief referred to in the discussion of India's diplomatic challenges?
x: Pakistan's army chief is Field Marshal Asim Munir.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the regional fallout of Operation Sindoor?
o: India treats Kashmir as a bilateral matter
The ceasefire was announced by US President Donald Trump
China reportedly backed India, creating a two-front threat for Pakistan
Pakistan's army chief is Field Marshal Asim Munir
x: China reportedly backed Pakistan, raising a two-front threat for India, not the reverse.

s: From 21 May 2025, how many multi-party delegations did India send abroad on cross-border terrorism after Operation Sindoor?
x: Seven multi-party delegations went to world capitals from 21 May 2025.

s: Nankana Sahib, to which India denied Sikh jathas in November 2025, is the birthplace of whom?
x: Nankana Sahib in Pakistan's Punjab is the birthplace of Guru Nanak (1469).

s: Which AP MP was part of the Operation Sindoor outreach delegation led by Shashi Tharoor to the USA, Panama, Guyana, Brazil and Colombia?
x: GM Harish Balayogi (TDP, Amalapuram) was in Shashi Tharoor's delegation to the Americas.

s: In which year was the Kartarpur Corridor opened?
x: The Kartarpur Corridor opened in 2019 and was suspended after Operation Sindoor in May 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the JCPOA and Iran's nuclear programme?
o: Germany was a party to the JCPOA
The United States withdrew from the JCPOA in 2019
Israel–US strikes hit Iranian nuclear sites in June 2025
x: The United States withdrew from the JCPOA in 2018, not 2019.

s: Which set of Iranian nuclear-related sites was targeted when the United States joined the Israel–Iran conflict in June 2025?
x: The targeted sites were Natanz, Fordow and Isfahan. Al-Udeid was later targeted by Iran in retaliation, while Qom and Tehran were not listed among the three sites struck by the United States.

s: The GBU-57 MOP used in the June 2025 strikes is best described as which of the following?
x: The GBU-57 MOP is a 30,000-pound conventional bunker buster. The solid-fuel missile was the Kheybar Shekan, while Tomahawk was a separate weapon.

s: Which country is not an NPT signatory and has no IAEA inspections of its undeclared nuclear arsenal?
x: Israel is not an NPT signatory and has no IAEA inspections; Iran was only debating an NPT-exit bill in June 2025.

s: Which Iranian site, struck in June 2025, was Iran's main uranium enrichment centre?
x: Natanz was the main enrichment centre; Fordow was the underground facility under a mountain near Qom.

s: In which country is the US Al-Udeid Air Base, struck by Iran in June 2025?
x: Iran struck Al-Udeid Air Base in Qatar with advance notice; the ceasefire was announced by Trump.

s: Which Article of the UN Charter bars the use of force?
x: Article 2 of the UN Charter bars the use of force.

s: At what level do the UN snapback sanctions reimposed on Iran in 2025 ban uranium enrichment?
x: The snapback measures include a ban on enrichment at any level, besides asset freezes, travel bans and an arms embargo.
